target_customer: Life science labs, lab managers and scientists in academia and biotech that order and track lab supplies
problem: Labs managed supply orders and inventory with spreadsheets, email and sticky notes; Quartzy centralizes requests, approvals, ordering and inventory.
business_model: Free lab management software monetized by supplier commissions on orders, later paid plans and marketplace
product_category: Lab management and life science supplies marketplace

founders.name: Adam Regelmann
founders.background_notes: YC page says he trained in internal medicine residency and faced the supply ordering problem in his own labs.

technical_complexity.rationale: Web ordering and inventory workflows with supplier catalog integrations; the hard part was fragmented vendor data (TechCrunch July 2011).

defensibility.rationale: Lab inventory data and approval workflows create switching costs, and supplier relationships took time to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; a 2015 TechCrunch piece said the space had little competition.

market_need_then: In July 2011 about 4,500 scientists used it and labs spend thousands of dollars on supplies each year (TechCrunch and YC blog, July 2011).

branding.community_and_virality: Won Business Insider's Startup 2011 competition per an aggregator summary (unverified); no merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in life science labs as a standard ordering tool, but no press about the brand beyond product coverage.

outcome_analysis: Quartzy built lab ordering and inventory software from founders who felt the problem in their own labs, grew to thousands of labs and raised Series A in 2013 and a $17M Series B in 2016. It reports over 28,000 customers on its site. No acquisition or layoffs were found; an April 2026 $23M financing was reported, labelled debt or other by some sources.
notes: TechCrunch 2016 states total raised nearly $25M with seed plus Series A combined $7.87M; the $1.2M seed (Feb 2012) rests on a single aggregator, so the seed and A recorded here do not sum to $7.87M and a gap remains. Series A date July 2013 from VC Post and Seedtable. The April 2026 $23M round is called Series A by raising.fi and pulse.bot, debt by Caplight; the label other is used and it rests on aggregator-type outlets. Totals vary from $27M to $53M across databases. No dated 2011 competitor was found: TechCrunch and the YC blog name none, and a 2015 TechCrunch piece names HappiLabs, which is too late. Founding year conflicts (2009, 2010, 2011); TechCrunch July 2011 says it launched about 18 months earlier.
